items.headline: Stocks end mixed Friday, but all three indexes win the week
items.note: On Nov. 13 the Dow rose 0.1% to about 52,348, while the S&P 500 fell 0.4% to about 7,562 and the Nasdaq 0.9% to about 25,136. For the week the S&P gained about 2.5%, the Nasdaq about 2.3% and the Dow about 2.1%, even with Nvidia and bond yields rattling Friday.

items.headline: Nvidia keeps sliding after Jensen Huang's exit; HSBC cuts it to Hold
items.note: Nvidia fell again Friday after a drop of more than 4% Thursday, closing with a market value under $4 trillion. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and earnings are due Tuesday, Nov. 17, the first big test of the post-Huang company.

items.headline: AMD, Broadcom and Intel drop sharply, reversing Thursday's rally
items.note: Reports put AMD down roughly 9–10%, Broadcom about 6% and Intel about 5% Friday. Yesterday these were seen as Nvidia share-gainers; today the whole chip group sold off, so leadership risk is spreading to the sector.

items.headline: Anthropic's IPO is expected to price the week of Nov. 16
items.note: Per Renaissance Capital, it is offering 825 million shares at $70–$78 on Nasdaq (ticker ANT), about $61 billion, plus a $26 billion private placement from firms like Google, Microsoft and Nvidia. It's the largest AI-lab listing yet and a test of public appetite for AI.

items.headline: Producer prices run at 6.5% a year; 10-year yield hits 5.17%
items.note: October producer prices rose 0.3% on the month, below the 0.4% expected, but the 12-month rate is the highest since November 2022. Traders expect a Fed rate hike next month, and the 10-year Treasury yield hit its highest since October, which pressures tech valuations.

items.headline: Bitcoin falls below $70,000 for the first time in nearly three months
items.note: It is down more than 20% so far this year, a sign of weak appetite for risk assets as yields climb. Worth watching if you're curious about how markets react to rate-hike fears.

items.headline: Tech sector added about 7,200 jobs in October; postings up 18.5% from a year ago
items.note: Per a summary of CompTIA's report, active tech postings reached 629,876 and AI skills dominate demand, but employers are hiring selectively. Specialized data/ML skills remain the in-demand ones for internship hunting.

items.headline: Anthropic signs its first news-licensing deal, with the Associated Press
items.note: Reported by Adweek via an AI newsletter (I couldn't open the original): Claude surfaced AP's real-time, attributed election data during the midterms. It shows how AI labs are starting to pay for fresh data.

items.headline: OpenAI reportedly made about $10 billion in revenue in one quarter, still at a large loss
items.note: Newsletter-reported and not independently confirmed by me. It frames the economics behind Anthropic's IPO: fast revenue growth paired with heavy compute spending.

learn.explain: The PPI measures how much prices change for the businesses that make and sell goods and services, before the products reach shoppers. It is an early signal: if companies pay more to produce things, they may pass those costs on to consumers, which shows up later in the CPI. Economists watch it alongside CPI because the Fed targets inflation. This week October PPI rose 0.3% on the month, less than the 0.4% forecast, but it was up 6.5% over twelve months, the highest since November 2022. Because the monthly figure beat expectations but the yearly one is high, markets still expect a Fed rate hike.
learn.try: Look up the latest CPI and PPI releases on the Bureau of Labor Statistics site and compare their yearly rates.
